days.title: Krafla Caldera Peaks and Craters
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Hlíðarfjall
stops.detail: On the outer edge of the caldera are, among others, two rhyolitic table volcanoes, Hlíðarfjall and Jörundur, which were formed under glaciers during the ice age.

stops.name: Leirhnjúkur
stops.detail: Tours of medium difficulty include those to Vindbelgjarfjall as well as around and onto Leirhnjúkur and from there down to the lake at Reykjahlíð in about five hours.

stops.name: Víti-Krater
stops.detail: Easy hikes lead, for example, on mostly wide paths through the remains of the lava lake at Dimmuborgir or around and onto the pseudocraters of Skútustaðir, as well as through the Hverarönd high-temperature area or to the Víti crater.

stops.name: Hverarönd
stops.detail: Solfataras and mud pools characterize the nearby high-temperature area Námaskarð or Hverarönd on the eastern side of the Námafjall volcano, which belongs to the Krafla system.

stops.name: Námafjall
stops.detail: Soon after, further series of eruptions followed in nearby fissures and also at Námafjall.
